macro_events.title: Iran peace-talk optimism collapses oil risk premium
macro_events.causal_chain: US-Iran diplomatic re-engagement reduces Hormuz blockade risk → war-risk insurance premiums on VLCCs ease → Brent -4.2% sub-$96, WTI -7% near $92 → lower jet fuel & gasoline inputs → airlines/consumer discretionary re-rate → energy majors give back risk premium → inflation expectations soften marginally, easing pressure on long end.
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Strait of Hormuz carries 21% of global oil and 20% of LNG; Qatar LNG flows to Europe depend on open transit. Asian refiners (India, South Korea) most sensitive to the spread.
macro_events.historical_analog: Sep 2019 Abqaiq attack reversal — Brent gave back 60% of spike within 10 sessions once Saudi capacity restored; similar mean-reversion setup if talks hold.
macro_events.counterargument: Talks have failed twice already; a single Houthi or IRGC tanker incident re-ignites the bid. Trump administration has not lifted Hormuz naval posture.

macro_events.title: Bear-steepener — 10Y at 4.29%, curve un-inverts after 27 months
macro_events.causal_chain: Fed on hold (3.50-3.75%) → front end anchored → long end pricing sticky core PCE 2.7% + Iran oil risk + Treasury supply concerns → 2s10s +54bp → banks benefit (NIM), long-duration tech faces multiple compression at margin, REITs pressured, gold consolidates at $445 GLD.
macro_events.geographic_dimension: USD strength moderates if Fed cuts materialize H2; EM rates exporters (EWZ, EEM) trail until dollar peaks.
macro_events.historical_analog: 2003 and 2013 bear-steepeners — equities held up until 10Y pushed decisively through psychological resistance (then 5%, now likely 4.75-5%).
macro_events.counterargument: A cooling labor print or disinflation surprise flattens the curve quickly; duration snaps back.
